reproduction: A bounded reverse probe launched a Guest TcpListener on 172.31.250.2:18182 through Invoke-Command -AsJob and attempted a Host TCP connect.
observation: Host-to-Guest TCP did not connect within 1.5 seconds; the remote listener job remained Running and its cleanup wrapper did not return promptly.
expected: A diagnostic listener should distinguish transport direction and terminate within the hard deadline without leaving a remote job.
impact: The probe confirms ordinary TCP is not usable on the isolated switch, but the diagnostic method itself introduced another remote-job cleanup risk.
evidence: HOST_TO_GUEST_CONNECTED=False and LISTENER_JOB_STATE=Running output; host wrapper session remained active.
optimization_location: communication adapter; do not use Invoke-Command -AsJob for recurring transport probes; use already-proven PowerShell Direct file/control transport or a purpose-built durable adapter.
minimal_change: Reap the exact probe wrapper/listener and redesign model egress over the existing Host↔Guest control/data channel rather than opening a Guest TCP path.
rollback: Remove only the temporary relay/firewall/listener artifacts after transport redesign is selected.
verification: No probe wrapper or listener remains; the chosen control/data adapter has a bounded request/response canary and durable result.
unresolved_risk: PowerShell Direct can transport files/commands but is not itself a streaming model proxy; the next adapter must preserve request/response streaming or use a Guest-side queue.
